newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares end IBIS DAX trade strongly ahead.
newsitem.headline: German shares end IBIS DAX trade strongly ahead.

text.p: German shares end bourse trade above the psychologically-important 2,900-point threshold, slightly off earlier highs, lifted by the strength of the dollar against the mark and firmer German debt.
The IBIS DAX index, which measures electronic trade in 30 German blue-chip stocks, closed at 2,904.08 points, up 27.74 points or 0.96 percent, only 11 points off an all-time high.

Earlier the DAX-30 index closed bourse trade at 2,906.34 points, up 20.21 points or 0.70 percent, a convincing breach of the 2,900-point marker deemed important by analysts for buoying market sentiment.
"We can't find any negative indicators out there -- we're still seeing net buyers and the market is looking very good," said one trader.
The dollar traded strongly firmer, standing at 1.5726 marks by the end of electronic trade.

Traders said that they were holding back from pushing the DAX towards any really significant gains as they waited to see U.S. rate implications of U.S. producer price and payroll data, due Thursday and Friday respectively.
The markets would also be closely monitoring German GDP and jobless data, due on Thursday morning, dealers said.
Banking shares were actively traded, benefiting from perennial takeover rumours in the sector and the apparent slow-down in the rally that chemical stocks saw in 1996.
Commerzbank AG in particular was strong, hitting a 12-month high over electronic trade, before coming off slightly to end the day up 1.17 pfennigs at 42.53 marks.
"The chemicals rally is over. Now the banks can finally take over the pole position," said one trader. Deutsche Bank, Germany's largest commercial bank, ended up 1.88 marks to 73.73.

At the same time, chemical stocks were generally lower at the end of the day. Hoechst AG was down 1.80 marks, nearly two percent, at 69.75 marks, BASF AG was down 28 pfennigs at 56.20 marks, and Bayer AG was down 23 pfennigs at 60 marks.
Auto stocks benefited from upbeat figures for the main German carmakers from the Detroit motor show.
"Bullish noises out of Detroit have been great for Volkswagen AG and Daimler-Benz AG," said one trader.
Volkswagen ended the day up 23.90 marks at 679.80 marks, while Daimler-Benz ended up 2.75 marks at 110.80 marks.
